title: Polynomial Optimization Over Unions of Sets
venue: Vietnam Journal of Mathematics 53:835–857 (2025); published online 24 July 2024
relevance: Primary source for the exact interval SOS contract. Section 4, equations (4.2)–(4.3): for h∈R[x]_{2d0} nonnegative on [a,b], h=p²+(x−a)(b−x)q² with deg p≤d0 and deg q≤d0−1. It allows zeros and preserves the degree cap. The odd-degree formula is also stated. The theorem is attributed to classical Lukács–Markov results; cite this source for the explicit nonnegative formula.
lane: global error bounds, quantitative-slack rational SOS, and ellipsoid contracts

title: Degree Bounds for Positivstellensätze of general semialgebraic sets
authors: Heijmans, Marieke and Kuryatnikova, Julia and Vera, Juan C. and Zuluaga, Luis F.
relevance: Primary May 2026 slack-lifting result. Theorem 2, §2.3: for normalized polynomial constraints on compact nonempty S_g⊂[-1,1]^n and f>0 on S_g, introduces one lift variable per constraint and a polynomial F with F(x,g(x))=f(x), degree at most max(deg f,2 deg g), and minimum at least f_min/2; its bound uses the global Łojasiewicz exponent and condition number. Theorem 4 gives an ordinary Putinar degree bound under 1−||x||²∈Q(g); Theorem 6 gives a full Schmüdgen preordering bound when S_g⊂(-1,1)^n. Conversion to the manuscript's distance-error exponent and extension of the lift to sparse bags are deductions, not stated sparse theorems in this paper.
lane: global error bounds, quantitative-slack rational SOS, and ellipsoid contracts

title: Squared polynomial approximation kernels for the hypercube: improved error bounds and implications for Lasserre hierarchies
authors: Gribling, Sander and de Klerk, Etienne and Vera, Juan C.
relevance: Primary dense approximation-kernel comparator for composing the lifted polynomial with an error bound. Theorem 7 gives a dense ordinary box quadratic-module gap at hierarchy index 2r bounded by c1 n^3 d^2 ||f||_{1,Cheb} log_2^3(r)/r^2, under its divisibility and lower-threshold conditions. It has no correlative sparsity or generator products. Combined with the May 2026 lift, the global-error rate O((log^{3/2} r/r)^alpha) follows as a deduction for dense modules; the sparse tree version with one lift variable per constraint is also a deduction, not a theorem stated here.
lane: global error bounds, quantitative-slack rational SOS, and ellipsoid contracts

title: On the convergence rates of moment-SOS hierarchies approximation of truncated moment sequences
authors: Tran, Hoang Anh and Toh, Kim-Chuan
relevance: Dense global-error-bound antecedent. Preprint Theorem 4.7 and Corollary 4.8 (numbering in arXiv:2507.00572v1) derive O(r^{-L}) approximation/objective bounds under compactness and their Łojasiewicz exponent L. Their reduced cone still includes inequality-subset products, and the result is not a sparse compatible bag construction. Cite preprint theorem numbering explicitly; journal publication appeared online 7 July 2026.
lane: global error bounds, quantitative-slack rational SOS, and ellipsoid contracts

title: Positive Univariate Polynomials: SOS certificates, algorithms, bit complexity, and T-systems
authors: Bender, Matías and Di Dio, Philipp and Tsigaridas, Elias
relevance: Closest direct polynomial-bit construction precedent found, but univariate. Theorem 2.14 (§2.4.3) constructs a strict-positivity SOS certificate on a rational interval [a,b] for integer input of degree d, coefficient bitsize τ, and endpoint bitsize σ in soft-O bit operations bounded by d³+d²σ+d²τ. The section gives rational coefficient bitsizes soft-O(dσ+dτ). The result does not establish the requested generic multivariate sparse Gram/SDP construction.
lane: global error bounds, quantitative-slack rational SOS, and ellipsoid contracts

title: Computing Sum of Squares Decompositions with Rational Coefficients
authors: Peyrl, Hans and Parrilo, Pablo A.
relevance: Classical numerical-to-exact rational Gram rounding result. Proposition 8, p. 276: if a numerical Gram matrix Q is at least εI, its distance to the coefficient affine space L is δ, and rational rounding gives Q~ within τ, then τ²+δ²≤ε² suffices for the exact orthogonal projection Π(Q~) to lie in L and remain PSD, yielding a rational SOS decomposition. This assumes a computed strictly feasible Gram matrix and an adequate numerical approximation; it is not an end-to-end polynomial-time Turing bound for generic multivariate SDP construction.
lane: global error bounds, quantitative-slack rational SOS, and ellipsoid contracts

title: On Exact Reznick, Hilbert-Artin and Putinar’s Representations
authors: Magron, Victor and Safey El Din, Mohab
relevance: Exact multivariate rational SOS antecedent under strict interior assumptions. Proposition 10 and Theorem 11 analyze the intsos algorithm for integer polynomials in the interior of the SOS cone and exact rational weighted SOS representations. The stated complexity is roughly τ² d^{d^{O(n)}} (with Newton-polytope refinements), generally doubly exponential in n rather than polynomial in expanded SDP dimension and log inverse slack. This is not the target generic sparse polynomial-bit guarantee.

title: Rational Dual Certificates for Weighted Sums-of-Squares Polynomials with Boundable Bit Size
relevance: Relevant bit-size and exact-algorithm precedent, with an important output distinction: Theorem 2.9 bounds rational weighted-SOS dual certificates; Theorem 4.1 and Algorithm 1 give a rational-arithmetic iterative method. These are dual membership certificates, not a generic primal rational Gram decomposition under a quantitative strict-slack promise.

title: Convex Optimization
venue: Cambridge University Press (2004), §5.3.2 and §5.3.6, printed pp. 234–236
relevance: Primary finite-dimensional convex duality contract. Slater feasibility gives zero duality gap; §5.3.6 states dual attainment when the optimal value is finite. For finite SDP, primal strict feasibility means satisfying the affine equations and each PSD block being positive definite; with a finite feasible primal optimum, the dual optimum is attained. If the full cone has no positive-definite feasible point, formulate Slater on the minimal face or use facial reduction rather than claiming full-cone Slater.
lane: global error bounds, quantitative-slack rational SOS, and ellipsoid contracts

title: Geometric Algorithms and Combinatorial Optimization
authors: Grötschel, Martin and Lovász, László and Schrijver, Alexander
venue: Algorithms and Combinatorics 2, Springer (1988), Chapter 3 §3.2, Theorem 3.2.1 and Lemma 3.2.8, printed pp. 87–90
relevance: Primary unknown-center ellipsoid source. Definition 2.1.16, p. 53, defines well-boundedness using a known inner radius whose ball center need not be explicitly known. Theorem 3.2.1 accepts a rational tolerance and a rational weak separation oracle; it returns a rational point in S(K,epsilon) or an enclosing rational ellipsoid of volume at most epsilon. Lemma 3.2.8 and theorem discussion bound the encoding lengths of rounded iterates and query points polynomially. To obtain an exact rational feasible point, supply a stronger oracle that accepts only exact feasible queries and otherwise returns valid rational cuts, and choose epsilon below a lower bound on the volume implied by the known inscribed radius. This exact-SDP conclusion is a composition, not the theorem’s weak-oracle output verbatim. Also bound oracle answer bit lengths for a Turing-time claim; the generic oracle theorem principally bounds arithmetic/query complexity.
lane: global error bounds, quantitative-slack rational SOS, and ellipsoid contracts

title: On the Turing model complexity of interior point methods for semidefinite programming
authors: de Klerk, Etienne and Vallentin, Frank
relevance: Important insufficient comparator for unknown-center feasibility. Theorem 1.1 assumes a known rational feasible matrix X0 and known rational radii r,R with X0+B(0,r) contained in the feasible set in its affine slice and the feasible set contained in X0+B(0,R). Its feasible-start hypothesis does not prove construction of that center from only an inner-radius promise; use Grötschel–Lovász–Schrijver §3.2 for that step.
lane: global error bounds, quantitative-slack rational SOS, and ellipsoid contracts
